samples.summary: The navigation guard can suppress the redirect that ejects a user from a document the server just refused them (403/404), and the redirect never retries
samples.evidence:
`NavigationGuardProvider` wraps every route in `App.tsx`, and its patched `navigator.push/replace` (navigation-guard-provider.tsx:132-135) asks the registered guards for *every* app-initiated navigation — including the ones that exist to eject a user whose access was withdrawn, not just sidebar clicks.

The five editors all redirect that way from inside the same subtree that mounts `SyncStatusChip`: document-detail.tsx:226-233, docs-detail.tsx:159-166, notes-detail.tsx:183, slides-detail.tsx:161, board-detail.tsx:125 all do `if (isDocumentError) { toast.error('Document not found'); navigate(fallbackSlug ? ... : '/documents', { replace: true }) }`. `isDocumentError` is how a 403/404 from `GET /documents/:id` surfaces — i.e. the document was deleted, moved out of reach, or the caller's permission was revoked while the tab sat open.

Attack/abuse chain: user A is editing a doc with unsent local edits (`mayHaveUnsent` true, so `useNavigationGuard` has a live guard registered — sync-status-chip.tsx:115). The owner revokes A's access. The next `document` query errors, the effect fires `navigate(..., {replace:true})`, which now routes through the patched navigator, `hasUnsentEdits()` returns a prompt, and the redirect is parked in `pendingRef` behind a Stay/Leave dialog (navigation-guard-provider.tsx:104-116). A clicks **Stay** → `pendingRef` is cleared (line 141-144) and, because the effect's deps are `[isDocumentError, navigate, fallbackSlug]` and none of them change again, nothing ever retries. A keeps rendering the document, keeps the Yorkie attachment, and keeps receiving collaborators' edits from a document they are no longer authorized for. The same code previously gave the user no choice.

This is only a client-side affordance where the Yorkie auth webhook is enforcing, but the repo's own comments say that enforcement is opt-in per deployment (`shared-document.tsx:1062-1066`: "a deployment must switch out of its default shadow mode (`YORKIE_AUTH_WEBHOOK_ENFORCE=true`) for a downgrade or a revocation to actually stop a write"). In a default deployment the client-side teardown is the only thing that ends the session, and this change makes it declinable.

Fix direction: give the guard an escape hatch for redirects that are not user-initiated (e.g. an option on `navigate` / a `bypassGuard` state flag, or re-firing the redirect after `stay()`), so authorization-driven navigations are never held back.

samples.summary: No test pins that a security-driven redirect (auth expiry / access revoked) is not held back by the new guard
samples.evidence: Both new suites only exercise user-initiated `<Link>` clicks (navigation-guard.test.tsx:63, sync-status-chip-navigation.test.tsx:97). Nothing asserts the behaviour of the guard against `<Navigate to="/login" replace />` (PrivateRoute.tsx:32, document-detail.tsx:863, docs-detail.tsx:342, notes-detail.tsx:369, board-detail.tsx:252, slides-detail.tsx:947, file-detail.tsx:242) or against the programmatic `navigate()` on `isDocumentError` (document-detail.tsx:229 and siblings). The unmount-before-effect ordering that currently saves the `<Navigate to="/login">` case is an implementation detail of React's passive-effect scheduling, not something this change states or tests, so a future refactor that keeps the chip mounted during the redirect would silently make the login redirect declinable too.
searchedFor: grep NavigationGuard|navigation-guard across packages/frontend (only the 2 new tests + the 3 source files + App.tsx)
grep isDocumentError|'Document not found' across packages/frontend (no test touches the redirect path except file-shell.test.tsx)

samples.summary: Forced logout on 401 uses `window.location.href`, which the unsent-edits `beforeunload` guard lets the user cancel — leaving an expired session rendered on screen
samples.evidence: `fetchWithAuth` handles an unrecoverable 401 by calling `logout({redirect:false,...})` then `redirectTo('/login')` (auth.ts:153-160), and `redirectTo` assigns `window.location.href` (auth.ts:27-31). When `SyncStatusChip`'s `beforeunload` handler is armed (sync-status-chip.tsx:92-103) the browser shows its leave-site prompt for that assignment, and the user can cancel it: the session cookie is already destroyed server-side, but the editor stays rendered with the document contents visible and no further redirect attempt (`isRedirecting` is now latched true, so no later call re-tries). Pre-existing rather than introduced here, but this change extends the same 'user may decline to leave' model to in-app navigation and the design doc claims parity between the two guards, so it is worth deciding deliberately: security-forced redirects should not be cancellable by a data-loss prompt.

verdict.reason: The described code exists exactly as quoted: the patched navigator intercepts every app-initiated push/replace (navigation-guard-provider.tsx:104-116,132-135), stay() drops pendingRef with no replay (141-144), and the isDocumentError eject uses navigate(..., {replace:true}) with deps that never re-fire (document-detail.tsx:226-233), with the guard registered by SyncStatusChip in the same subtree (site-header.tsx:108, sync-status-chip.tsx:115-131). It is nonetheless not a Security-lens defect. (a) The redirect is not an enforced authorization path — enforcement already occurred server-side in the 403/404 that set isDocumentError; suppressing the client redirect yields no data the server has not already refused, only the local replica the user already held. (b) The principal clicking "Stay" is the same principal whose access was revoked, so nothing is bypassed that the user could not achieve by simply not navigating away; a control the adversary declines for himself is not an access boundary. (c) The finding's load-bearing premise that Yorkie enforcement defaults to shadow mode is false in this repo: isYorkieAuthEnforced returns true unless the literal string "false" is set (yorkie-auth-enforcement.ts:29-31, "Enforcing is the default", echoed in yorkie-auth.controller.ts:120-143 and self-hosting.md:589-592); the shared-document.tsx:1062-1066 comment it cites is stale prose, not behavior. With the webhook methods registered PushPull/Watch are server-gated; without registration Yorkie gates nothing for anyone, independent of this redirect. (d) I checked the genuinely security-relevant navigations for a bypass: the /login ejections are <Navigate> rendered above the guarded subtree (document-detail.tsx:863, PrivateRoute.tsx:32), so the chip unmounts and deregisters in the same commit and those are never held. The remaining issue — a dropped redirect that never retries, leaving stale UI — is real but belongs to the correctness lens, not authorization/secrets/injection/crypto.
